questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes audio watermarking from anti-spoofing detection?

options.A: Watermarking proves the spoken words are factually accurate.
options.B: Anti-spoofing detection requires every generator to embed a payload.
options.C: Both methods require the original reference waveform at detection time.
options.D: Watermarking embeds a detectable signal; anti-spoofing estimates whether audio is synthetic.

questions.explanation: Watermarking adds a signal during generation. Anti-spoofing classifies audio and can be applied to outputs from generators that do not cooperate.

questions.text: Your watermark detector finds no watermark in an uploaded recording. What conclusion is justified?

options.A: The recording is certainly authentic human speech.
options.B: No watermark was detected; this alone does not establish authenticity.
options.C: The recording must be synthetic because metadata was removed.
options.D: The speaker’s identity has been cryptographically verified.

questions.explanation: Synthetic audio may never have been watermarked, or the watermark may be damaged or missed. Absence of detection is not proof of authenticity.

questions.text: spectral_rolloff sets threshold = 0.85 * sum(spec), accumulates from index 0, and returns the first index where cum >= threshold. For spec = [1, 1, 6, 2], which index is returned?
questions.explanation: The threshold is 8.5. Cumulative sums are 1, 2, 8, 10; index 3 is the first to reach it.
